title: Heuristic-driven KV slice allocator and prefill prioritization for paged attention
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: As paged attention is used across mixed workloads (chat, long-context retrieval, embeddings prefill), the KV cache experiences fragmentation and imbalanced prefill priority. This leads to suboptimal kernel selection (mismatched micro-batches on GPU), unnecessary prefill work for low-reuse keys, and increased 95th percentile latency during decode.

Goal: Implement a lightweight, heuristic-driven KV segmentation (slice) allocator and a prefill prioritization layer that: (1) groups KV entries into slices by reuse likelihood and kernel compatibility, (2) enforces soft quotas per-tenant/sess to reduce cross-tenant eviction storms, and (3) drives a prefill scheduler that matches prefills to kernels with compatible batch shapes to improve throughput and reduce tail latency.

Constraints: Must be incremental (feature flagged), low CPU overhead in control plane, compatible with existing paged storage format, and safe for Dedicated/Private deployments where memory budgets are strict. No model changes. Prefer heuristics that are explainable and tunable from Console.

Proposed approach summary:
- KV slice definition: each slice is a contiguous allocation class representing a recency/use-score bucket and a kernel-compatibility tag (e.g., short-seq vs long-seq kernels, 8-bit quant paths).
- Heuristic scoring: compute per-key score = w1*recency + w2*access_frequency + w3*expected_reuse (based on session type) + w4*kernel_match_score. Scores are discretized into 4 slices (hot/warm/cold/archival).
- Allocation policy: allocate new KV pages into the slice whose headroom and kernel tag matches; slices have configurable soft quotas and eviction priority order (cold-first).
- Eviction: on reclaim, prefer cross-slice compaction where small cold fragments can be batched for eviction, minimizing fragmentation of hot slices.
- Prefill prioritizer: maintain a prioritized queue of prefill candidates scored by cache-miss penalty * reuse-likelihood; batch prefills by kernel tag to produce better micro-batches; optionally delay low-value prefills during tail risk windows.
- Kernel selection synergy: surface kernel compatibility tag from slice metadata to downstream kernel selector so it can choose the best kernel variant without per-request profiling.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Heuristic misclassification can cause premature eviction of useful keys; mitigate with conservative defaults and short probation periods.
- Additional metadata per KV entry increases footprint; we will encode tags compactly (bitfields) and measure overhead.
- Multitenant fairness can reduce peak throughput if quotas are too strict; will tune via traffic experiments.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end rollout behind feature flag with Canary on 10% of traffic.
2) 95th-percentile decode latency reduction >= 12% for mixed chat+retrieval workload in benchmark harness (compare baseline runtime-1.19).
3) Measured fragmentation index (free-span count / total-pages) reduced by >= 25% after compaction pass within 24 hours of steady traffic.
4) No regression (>1%) in average token throughput for production-like benchmarks.
5) Console exposes two knobs: slice thresholds and per-tenant soft-quota, with audit logs for slice evictions.
6) Automated tests covering slice assignment, eviction ordering, and prefill batching correctness.
implementation_notes:
Phase 1 (PoC): add compact slice tag (2 bits) and a 1-byte score histogram in the KV page header. Implement allocator that chooses page pools by tag and updates metadata on promote/demote. Integrate with the existing prefill queue service to add a kernel_tag field.
Phase 2: implement eviction compactor that can coalesce cold fragments across adjacent pages before freeing. Add configuration surfaces in Console and runtime flags for Dedicated/Private memory budgets.
Phase 3: add metrics and cost counters per-slice and a feedback loop that adjusts slice thresholds based on observed reuse.

Integration points: kv-pager, prefill-queue, kernel-selector, console-config.

Backward compatibility: old pages without tags should be treated as "warm" during first sweep and assigned tags lazily on access.
testing_plan:
Unit tests: slice assignment logic, score discretization, eviction ordering.
Integration tests: synthetic workload with interleaved short and long sequences to validate kernel batching and prefill coalescing.
Load tests: run the 1M request benchmark harness with mixed tenants and measure p50/p95/p99 decode latency and throughput.
Chaos tests: force page pressure and validate soft-quota fairness across tenants.
Canary plan: 10% traffic for 48 hours -> 30% for 72 hours -> full rollout. Metrics monitored: p95 decode latency, fragmentation index, evictions/sec, token throughput, and memory overhead.
rollout: Feature flagged behind runtime.prefill_slices. Start on internal staging, then Canary on small customer subset (non-enterprise) to minimize SLA risk. Use runtime-1.20 release and provide a rollback kill-switch via Console.
